name: Devil’s Mother

attributes.attribute: borne by a large squat mountain in northern Connemara
fearsome serpent who battled Saint Patrick

sources: MacNeill, Máire. The Festival of Lughnasa, Parts I and II. Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982, 400.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Devil's Mother is an Irish goddess or heroine. Her names include Kiraghna and Keeronagh. Male gods sometimes appear as the Devil in Christian thought. Goddesses met a similar fate. People transformed them into demonic forces. Those people wished to deter continued worship. Some Irish goddesses earned the name Devil's Mother. A large squat mountain bore the name. The mountain stands in northern Connemara. Connemara is in the western province of Connacht. Two characters also bear the name. Both fought the arriving Saint Patrick. Corra was a bird-fiend. Caoranach was a fearsome serpent. The mountain and the creatures tie the Devil's Mother to the Irish land. Each bearer fought the saint's arrival. Each failed in turn. The title linked the old goddesses to resistance. It kept their memory alive in a Christian frame.
objective: Describe the Irish goddess-heroine Devil's Mother and her bearers.
key_results: Give the names Kiraghna and Keeronagh
Explain how Christianization made goddesses demonic
